discovery.none: Manual selection only. No advertised OP-Z local name was established by the research. The standard BLE-MIDI service is present on unrelated keyboards, controllers and adapters, so its UUID must not auto-select this spec. device.name: teenage engineering OP-Z
device.notes: OP-Z is a 16-track multimedia sequencer and synthesizer. This initial spec deliberately covers standard BLE-MIDI, the official incoming MIDI map, midi.json configuration, and documented USB/app lifecycle procedures. It does not expose proprietary app visual/content commands. Local MIDI and USB content backup do not require a cloud account. No latest-firmware claim or universal host-pairing rule is made.

openness.notes: The vendor documents MIDI behavior and lifecycle procedures. The official app's transport was also inspected to establish the standard GATT UUIDs, notification setup and BLE-MIDI header handling. No vendor-specific radio opcode or app-internal protocol is included.

steps.action: Open the official app's devices screen and start a scan if the platform requires one.
Press the pair button on the back of OP-Z.
Select the intended OP-Z in the app list to connect.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the existing app/MIDI client, manually select the intended unit, and retry. For the official app, use the rear pair button again. Do not factory-reset merely to work around an unproven bond conflict.

pairing.notes: No universal pairing, bonding, single-connection or single-bond claim is made. The official guide documents an app discovery/pair-button flow; independent MIDI host link-layer behavior still needs hardware checks.

unpair.notes: No bond-only clearing procedure is established. Factory reset removes custom content and must not be presented as a benign unpair shortcut.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi credential, account token or MIDI API key is documented. Any OS-level bond records and app-specific content are outside this spec's credential claims.

factory_reset.description: Factory reset is initiated in upgrade mode, not content mode and not by a MIDI message. It is destructive. Back up user content first and safely eject before power cycling. The final indicator differs from the initial upgrade-mode indicator, as detailed in the procedure steps.
factory_reset.effect: Restores original factory settings and removes custom user content. Whether every host-specific Bluetooth bond is cleared is not separately established.

procedures.basis: Official OP-Z user/disk-mode guide v1.2.45 sections 22.6 and 22.8; not executed by this project.
procedures.description: Enter upgrade mode first, then hold screen and stop together for one second. Custom user content is removed.
procedures.indicator: A blinking white LED and four green LEDs when the reset finishes.
procedures.name: Screen and stop in upgrade mode

steps.action: Back up any content you need to keep, then start with OP-Z off.
Hold the screen button while turning OP-Z on.
steps.expect: Upgrade mode: the kick LED blinks white and all parameter-dial LEDs are white.

steps.action: With OP-Z in upgrade mode, hold screen and stop together for one second.
steps.expect: A blinking white LED and four green LEDs indicate that the factory reset has finished.

steps.action: Safely eject OP-Z, power cycle it, and verify that it restarts ready for setup.

methods.basis: Official OP-Z MIDI guide and official app 1.3.3 standard BLE-MIDI transport; not replayed against hardware.
methods.description: Use ordinary timestamped BLE-MIDI in both directions. All 16 tracks can send and receive MIDI, subject to the instrument's per-track and global settings. No app-specific authentication or command is added.
methods.name: Standard BLE-MIDI performance

steps.action: Manually select the intended OP-Z; never auto-select a peripheral solely because it advertises the generic MIDI service.
If MIDI input or output is disabled, hold tempo and screen together and use key 2 for incoming MIDI or key 3 for outgoing MIDI, checking the resulting setting rather than blindly toggling it twice.
Connect and locate service 03b80e5a-ede8-4b33-a751-6ce34ec4c700 and characteristic 7772e5db-3868-4112-a1a9-f2669d106bf3.
Read the MIDI characteristic as the official app does, then enable notifications and the client-characteristic configuration descriptor.
Keep MIDI message and running-status state across notifications; strip BLE-MIDI headers/timestamps and emit only complete messages.

methods.basis: Official OP-Z app guide section 23.2; the physical flow was not run.
methods.description: Pair the official companion app using the rear pair button. This is the documented app route and does not establish a universal bonding requirement for independent BLE-MIDI hosts.
methods.name: Official OP-Z app pairing

steps.action: Open the official app's devices screen. On platforms that need it, start the BLE scan; Android requires location-services permission for BLE connection.
Press the pair button on the back of OP-Z.
When the intended OP-Z appears in the app device list, tap it to connect.
For app configuration, use the documented MIDI setup screen; do not infer proprietary visual/content commands from this standard-MIDI spec.

methods.basis: Official OP-Z disk-mode guide section 22.2 and MIDI guide section 21.4; not run on hardware.
methods.description: Use the removable USB disk to back up or restore projects, samples, bounces and configuration, including midi.json. This is separate from BLE-MIDI performance and from upgrade mode.
methods.name: USB content-mode configuration and backup

steps.action: With OP-Z off, hold the track button while turning it on.
steps.expect: All track LEDs are green, indicating content mode.

steps.action: Connect OP-Z to a computer with a USB data cable and open the removable OP-Z disk.
Back up the disk before changes. Edit midi.json only using the documented setting names and ranges; its detailed JSON container shape is not asserted here.
Safely eject the disk before unplugging. Changes are applied while OP-Z synchronizes and restarts in normal mode.
Wait for synchronization and restart to finish; do not power off during that process.

setup.notes: Ordinary MIDI needs no account or provisioning. Enable incoming/outgoing MIDI on the instrument as needed, manually select the peripheral, and use the standard service. The official app has a separate rear-button pairing flow. USB content mode is an independent local route for configuration and backup, not a proprietary BLE command channel.

rejoin.notes: A new standard-MIDI host is selected manually. For the official app, repeat the rear pair-button flow. Factory reset is destructive and is not the routine way to change hosts; no separate unpair procedure is established.

testing.notes: No OP-Z was connected, reset, updated or driven by this project. Standard BLE-MIDI facts are reported from the official MIDI/user guides and the official Android app 1.3.3 transport implementation. The official guide procedures are unexecuted. BLE-MIDI test vectors are synthetic standard- library constructions checked by scripts/test_teenage_engineering_op_z.py, not captured device traffic.

evidence.app_static_analysis: The official Android app 1.3.3 (601766) transport uses the standard MIDI service and characteristic, reads the characteristic, enables notifications and CCCD, and implements standard BLE-MIDI header/timestamp handling. Its 240-byte outgoing allocation and 1024-byte decoder allocation are recorded only as implementation observations. No proprietary command surface is inferred or exposed.

BleMidiPacket.description: Standard BLE-MIDI packet structure, not a fixed-length OP-Z payload. Byte 0 is a header with bits 10 followed by six timestamp-high bits. Subsequent high-bit bytes are seven-bit timestamp-low bytes when the parser is expecting a timestamp; the following MIDI byte can be a status or a data byte. Full state rules are in protocol_details.ble_midi.

fields.description: Required bits 10 plus timestamp high bits; header & 0xc0 == 0x80.
fields.name: header

fields.description: Interleaved timestamp-low and MIDI bytes, continuing across packets when necessary.
fields.name: packet_body

parse_rules: Compute a timestamp as ((header & 0x3f) << 7) | (timestamp_low & 0x7f), modulo 8192 ms; timestamp bytes never enter the MIDI message.
Do not treat each notification as one MIDI message. Preserve the current message, SysEx state and channel running status across notifications.
Use protocol_details.ble_midi.receive_reassembly and the synthetic vectors rather than assuming a notification boundary or a fixed MTU.

outgoing: Packetize complete MIDI messages with standard BLE-MIDI header/timestamp bytes and negotiated ATT payload limits. Preserve message order and standard running-status rules.
A long SysEx may span writes; do not start each write with F0, and place F7 only at the actual end. A continuation write still has a BLE-MIDI packet header.
The official app's 240-byte write-packet allocation is not a guaranteed OP-Z or host MTU. Negotiate and honor the actual connection limit.
receive_reassembly: Keep current_message, expected channel/system data-byte count, in_sysex and running_status across notifications. Reset them only on disconnect or a deliberate parser reset.

After removing the notification header, walk the body. A low-bit byte is MIDI data for the pending message (or for running status); a high-bit byte consumed as a timestamp never enters current_message.
Channel statuses 8x, 9x, Ax, Bx and Ex take two data bytes; Cx and Dx take one. Preserve channel running status so a timestamp may be followed by data without a repeated status.

F0 starts SysEx and clears channel running status. Buffer all following MIDI data across notifications through F7 and emit the SysEx only when complete. F1/F3 take one data byte, F2 takes two, and F6 takes none; these system-common messages clear running status.

F8 through FF are zero-data real-time statuses and do not clear channel running status. Deliver one immediately even when it appears inside an incomplete SysEx, without inserting it into the SysEx payload.
A new notification may begin with continuation data below 80, or with a timestamp. It need not begin with a MIDI status. Conversely, several complete messages may be coalesced into one notification.

Reject an unexpected data byte with neither a pending message nor running status, and reject a new non-real-time status that interrupts an incomplete message rather than emitting a plausible truncated message.
Bound partial-message/SysEx buffers in a production client. The official app's 1024-byte decoder allocation is an implementation observation, not a protocol maximum.
ble_midi.scope: Standard BLE-MIDI and standard MIDI messages only. OP-Z-specific behavior is limited to the official incoming map and configuration below. No proprietary commands are included.

test_vectors.description: Constructed from standard BLE-MIDI rules to test stateful reassembly. notifications_hex are GATT payloads; messages_hex are complete MIDI messages after timestamps are removed. No vector is an OP-Z capture.

realtime_inside_sysex.notes: The real-time clock is emitted immediately; the SysEx is emitted only when its F7 arrives.

timestamp_rules: Every notification begins with a header for which byte & 0xc0 == 0x80. Its low six bits are timestamp high bits.
When expecting a timestamp, a high-bit body byte supplies the low seven timestamp bits and is not MIDI data. The next body byte is MIDI even when it is another high-bit status byte.

The timestamp is ((high & 0x3f) << 7) | low, modulo 8192 ms. If the low value decreases from the preceding timestamp WITHIN THE SAME NOTIFICATION, advance the high group by 128 modulo 8192. Reset that comparison at each new notification and trust its header; never advance the high group merely because the previous packet ended with a larger low value.
Timestamps may order/schedule events but do not delimit SysEx or substitute for MIDI message-length state.

device_midi_settings.access: Hold tempo and screen together, then use the corresponding key; track-channel assignment uses a held track button and the green dial.
device_midi_settings.notes: These are toggles, so inspect the current result rather than sending a blind sequence. Incoming clock automatically selects external sync. Outgoing MIDI must be enabled before a host can rely on performance data.

toggles.setting: mute all MIDI on the corresponding track
set that track's MIDI channel to 1-16

other_and_realtime.name: clock
other_and_realtime.notes: Incoming clock automatically selects external sync; four green LEDs show tempo while tempo is held.

incoming_midi.scope: All 16 tracks can send and receive MIDI, with per-track channels and configurable outgoing CC assignments. Channels and values below reproduce the official incoming table. Any means the setting is not channel-bound. Relative entries document only values 1 and 127; this spec does not infer which value increments or decrements.

Back up the existing disk/file and preserve its established JSON structure while changing only documented settings.

settings.meaning: Redirect incoming MIDI channel 1 to the currently active track.
True: bank 1-16 / program 1-16 selects the active pattern. False: bank 1 / program 1-128 and bank 2 / program 1-32 select patterns 1-160.
Echo incoming MIDI on the same port and through to other ports.
Enable MIDI on the corresponding track.
Assign the outgoing CC value. The official range is 0-255; do not silently substitute a different range.

Safely eject the USB disk.

characteristics.name: Standard BLE-MIDI I/O
characteristics.notes: The official app reads, writes and enables notifications on this characteristic. BLE-MIDI notifications and writes are packets, not guaranteed complete MIDI messages. A message may continue in the next packet and one packet may contain several messages. Write-side segmentation must use standard BLE-MIDI timestamps and the negotiated ATT payload; the app's 240-byte buffer is not a universal MTU claim.

services.name: Standard BLE-MIDI service
services.notes: Standard timestamped MIDI only. This service is deliberately not an automatic OP-Z identity signal. No vendor-specific characteristic, SysEx command, visual-module protocol or authentication command is declared by this spec.
